The tensile testing is performed on two batches of specimens. The first batch of specimens correspond to the coupons obtained from overmolding of 40% wt. CF/PA66 on triangular metallic lattice in a small mold (6” x 6”). The second batch of tensile specimens are obtained by overmolding 20% wt. CF/ABS on the binder jet metal inserts with start shaped hooks for enabling better mechanical interlocking. The fabrication of both these set of specimens were entailed in Section 3.3) 5.3.1 Tensile characteristics of maraging steel overmolded with CF/PA66 Experimental Investigation The overmolded panel (6” x 6”) shown in Fig. 5.3.1.1(a) was machined to obtain coupon specimens with custom dimensions as shown in Fig. 5.3.1.1(b). Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests were performed on coupon specimens shown in Fig. 5.3.1.1(b) at an applied nominal rate of 0.0012 𝑠−1 using an extensometer to determine the strain. The resulting stress-strain curves are shown in Fig. 5.3.1.2(a). The average elastic modulus, tensile strength, and strain to failure were determined to be 9.1 ± 0.6 GPa, 76.4 ± 7 MPa, and 1.21% respectively. In the existing works, the average tensile strength of metal-polymer bonds is either 30 MPa using chemical etching process [11] or 23 MPa through integrated laser powder bed fusion and fused filament fabrication process [10]. Compared to these, the tensile strength of the hybrid structures fabricated through additive manufacturing – compression molding process are 2-3x higher. In addition, the control over fiber alignment through deposition pattern [12, 1] and design of 2D/3D lattice structures [13,14,15] would enable tunable mechanical properties for the hybrid structures manufactured via this process.
